citations.assessment: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak identifies Mar son of Ravina as reconciling the two views on blessing over bread. Heilprin has an inclusive phrase where the retrieved witness says both.
The same introductory formula concerns the order of putting on shoes. This witness spells the patronymic Ravna.
The two adjacent stories describe a newly created spring and finding shelter from the camel. The wall opened so that Mar could enter.
Tosafot on Berakhot expressly interprets the Bavli passage as referring to a dream-fast. Beit Yosef quotes a comparable Rashba interpretation.
The cited Bavli directly gives Shavuot, Purim and the eve of Yom Kippur. Heilprin’s two modern punctuation possibilities remain in the translation and notes.
The Bavli gives seven outfits for seven days. The immediately adjacent line is Rava’s statement about a louse affecting his study. Heilprin combines that rationale with the garment notice.

Three adjacent units give distinct details. Mar breaks a 400-zuz cup in the first story. Rav Ashi breaks a white-glass cup in the second. Rav Hamnuna sings at the wedding of Mar son of Ravina in the third. Heilprin groups the two cup details together.
